analysis.title: Magna International Inc. (MGA): 3Q26 First Take
key_insights: Magna reported 3Q26 adjusted EBIT of $683 mn and adjusted EPS of $1.83, above the Street ($623 mn / $1.58) and GS ($611 mn / $1.51). Revenue was $10.1 bn, in line with the Street at $10.1 bn and slightly below GS at $10.2 bn.
3Q26 revenue was down 8% qoq, down 4% yoy and down 2% organically. Magna said it grew 0.5% over its weighted markets, or 1% excluding Complete Vehicles.
Adjusted EBIT margin was 6.8% vs GS at 6.0% and the Street at 6.2%. Body Exteriors & Structures margin was 9.3% (GS 8.0%) and Power & Vision margin was 7.6% (GS 6.3%).

Magna lowered CY26 revenue guidance to $41.2-42.0 bn ($41.6 bn midpoint, down 1% yoy) from $41.3-42.5 bn ($41.9 bn midpoint, about flat yoy), citing lower expected China vehicle production and program mix.

CY26 adjusted EBIT margin guidance is 6.3%-6.5% (from 6.3%-6.6%), in line with the Street and GS at 6.4%. The EPS range is $6.85-$7.15 (from $6.70-$7.30), with the midpoint of $7.00 maintained. Magna expects lower net interest expense and a lower tax rate.

Implied 4Q26 guidance at the midpoint is well below expectations: revenue $10.2 bn, adjusted EBIT $745 mn, margin 7.3% and EPS $1.93, vs GS at $10.6 bn / $867 mn / 8.2% / $2.27 and the Street at $10.5 bn / $832 mn / 7.9% / $2.23.

Capital spending guidance for CY26 is about $1.5 bn (from $1.5-1.6 bn). FCF guidance was raised to $1.85-1.90 bn from $1.75-1.85 bn. 3Q adjusted FCF was about $584 mn, with $129 mn of dividends and $529 mn of share repurchases.
GS keeps a Sell rating on MGA with a 12-month price target of $55 (7x normalized EPS of $7.90 including SBC), implying 15.0% downside from $64.70. The MG.TO target is C$77.
Expected call topics: Magna's ability to outgrow the market, margins (efficiency efforts and cost inflation), the demand environment and capital allocation.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q beat on EBIT and EPS, but implied 4Q guidance is 10-14% below the Street on EBIT and EPS, and CY26 revenue guidance was cut on weaker China production and mix. The $55 target implies 15.0% downside from $64.70.

sector_views.rationale: GS rates Magna Sell relative to its coverage universe, with 15% downside to its target.

earnings_insights: MGA 3Q26 reported 10/30: revenue $10.1 bn (Street $10.1 bn, GS $10.2 bn), non-GAAP EBIT $683 mn (Street $623 mn, GS $611 mn), non-GAAP EPS $1.83 (Street $1.58, GS $1.51).
MGA 3Q26 non-GAAP EBIT margin was 6.8% reported vs GS 6.0% and Street 6.2%, a beat of 80 bps vs GS and 60 bps vs the Street.
MGA CY26 guidance (company, issued 10/30): revenue $41.2-42.0 bn (GS estimate $42.1 bn, Street $41.9 bn), adjusted EBIT margin 6.3%-6.5%, adjusted EPS $6.85-$7.15 (GS estimate $7.00, Street $7.05).

MGA implied 4Q26 guidance at the midpoint: revenue $10.2 bn, adjusted EBIT $745 mn, margin 7.3%, adjusted EPS $1.93, vs GS estimates of $10.6 bn / $867 mn / 8.2% / $2.27 and Street (FactSet) estimates of $10.5 bn / $832 mn / 7.9% / $2.23.
GS estimates for MGA EPS: $7.00 for CY26E, $7.60 for CY27E and $8.20 for CY28E. 4Q26E EPS is $2.27 and 1Q27E is $1.26.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Magna cut its China production assumption, a main reason for the lower revenue guidance.
Unchanged assumption, so the guidance cut is not driven by North America.
Unchanged assumption, so the guidance cut is not driven by Europe.

risk_factors: Upside risks to the Sell call: Magna gaining share, including with key customers and in Asia.
Upside risks: content per vehicle growth that outpaces industry production, and an earlier profitable pivot to megatrend growth areas.
Upside risks: faster EBIT margin and FCF improvement than GS estimates.
Upside risks: a better auto cycle or demand environment, or more favorable tariff rules than expected.
Downside risks reflected in guidance: lower China production and unfavorable program mix.
